# tritonctl sandbox fs

Files in a sandbox

Subcommands: put, get, cat, mv, mkdir, ls, stat, rm, watch

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox fs [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

## tritonctl sandbox fs put

Copy a local file into the sandbox

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox fs put [OPTIONS] <SANDBOX> <LOCAL> <PATH>`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix
- `<LOCAL>`: Local file, or `-` for stdin
- `<PATH>`: Absolute path in the sandbox
- `--mode <MODE>`: File mode, in octal (`644`)
- `--user <USER>`: Guest user that owns the file

## tritonctl sandbox fs get

Copy a file out of the sandbox

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox fs get [OPTIONS] <SANDBOX> <PATH> [LOCAL]`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix
- `<PATH>`: Absolute path in the sandbox
- `<LOCAL>`: Local file to write. Stdout when omitted or `-`
- `--user <USER>`: Guest user to read as

## tritonctl sandbox fs cat

Print a file in the sandbox to stdout

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox fs cat [OPTIONS] <SANDBOX> <PATH>`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix
- `<PATH>`: Absolute path in the sandbox
- `--user <USER>`: Guest user to read as

## tritonctl sandbox fs mv

Move a path. An existing destination is replaced

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox fs mv [OPTIONS] <SANDBOX> <SOURCE> <DESTINATION>`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix
- `<SOURCE>`: Absolute path to move
- `<DESTINATION>`: Absolute path to move it to
- `--user <USER>`: Guest user to act as

## tritonctl sandbox fs mkdir

Make a directory and any missing parents

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox fs mkdir [OPTIONS] <SANDBOX> <PATH>`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix
- `<PATH>`: Absolute path in the sandbox
- `--mode <MODE>`: Directory mode, in octal (`755`)
- `--user <USER>`: Guest user that owns the directory

## tritonctl sandbox fs ls

List a directory

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox fs ls [OPTIONS] <SANDBOX> <PATH>`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix
- `<PATH>`: Absolute path in the sandbox

## tritonctl sandbox fs stat

Show one path

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox fs stat [OPTIONS] <SANDBOX> <PATH>`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix
- `<PATH>`: Absolute path in the sandbox

## tritonctl sandbox fs rm

Remove a path

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox fs rm [OPTIONS] <SANDBOX> <PATH>`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix
- `<PATH>`: Absolute path in the sandbox
- `-r, --recursive`: Remove a directory and everything in it

## tritonctl sandbox fs watch

Print changes under a path until interrupted

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox fs watch [OPTIONS] <SANDBOX> <PATH>`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix
- `<PATH>`: Absolute path in the sandbox
- `-r, --recursive`: Watch every directory below the path too
